jobs.title: Project Controls Director
jobs.description:
Overview

AtkinsRéalis is seeking a highly experienced Project Controls Director to lead integrated project controls on a major capital infrastructure project delivered through a collaborative delivery model. As a key member of the integrated project leadership team, you will work alongside clients, delivery partners, designers, contractors, and stakeholders to align scope, schedule, cost, risk, change, commercial performance, and reporting.

This role offers the opportunity to shape project outcomes through data-driven decision-making, transparent governance, and collaborative leadership. If you are passionate about delivering complex engineering and infrastructure projects while driving innovation, accountability, and project excellence, we want to hear from you.

Your Role

Lead integrated project controls across the project leadership team, ensuring alignment between clients, delivery partners, designers, contractors, and commercial teams.
Develop and govern a single integrated project controls framework, including baselines, data standards, reporting processes, and accountability structures.
Facilitate integrated planning, schedule development, milestone alignment, and forecasting activities across multiple organizations.
Lead the management of cost, schedule, risk, opportunity, change, and performance reporting to support project objectives and key performance indicators.
Provide performance insights, scenario analysis, and option evaluations to support evidence-based decision-making and project optimization.
Develop integrated dashboards, reports, and executive presentations that provide a common source of truth for project teams and governance forums.
Lead, mentor, and develop multidisciplinary project controls teams while driving continuous improvement, collaboration, and knowledge sharing.

About You

Ability to lead project controls functions on large, complex capital or infrastructure projects with a minimum of 15 years of relevant experience.
Proficiency in integrated planning and scheduling, cost management, risk and opportunity management, change control, forecasting, performance measurement, and executive reporting.
Ability to establish integrated project controls processes, shared data environments, common baselines, and transparent reporting frameworks across multiple organizations.
Aptitude for influencing senior stakeholders, facilitating collaborative decision-making, resolving conflicts, and building alignment within complex project environments.
Proficiency in project controls systems, PMIS platforms, common data environments, data visualization tools, and reporting software.

Rewards & Benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career at AtkinsRéalis in Canada.

Enjoy competitive compensation, employee recognition, and a brilliant range of flexible benefits you can tailor to your health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle needs.

Make the most of diverse opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise.

And take advantage of our hybrid working culture and generous time-off policies to balance a fulfilling career with your personal life.

Be rewarded. Find out more.

About AtkinsRéalis

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

Find out more.

Additional Information

AtkinsRéalis cares about your privacy. AtkinsRéalis and other subsidiary or affiliated companies of AtkinsRéalis (referred to throughout as "AtkinsRéalis") are committed to protecting your privacy. Please consult our Privacy Notice on our Careers site to know more about how we collect, use, and transfer your Personal Data.

By submitting your personal information to AtkinsRéalis, you confirm that you have read and accept our Privacy Notice.(Insert this link on the words: Privacy Notice https://careers.atkinsrealis.com/en/site-services/privacy-statement)

Appropriate accommodations will be provided upon request throughout the recruitment and hiring process as required by Company policy and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA).

Successful applicants will be notified about AtkinsRéalis' accommodation policies at the time the employment offer is extended, and the information will be shared with new personnel during the onboarding process.

jobs.company: the WIRELESS kiosk @Costco / le kiosque SANS-FIL @Costco
jobs.title: Director
jobs.description:
Why You’ll Love Working Here

About Us

As Canada’s # 1 retailer of cell phones, The Wireless Kiosk @ Costco operates in every Canadian warehouse coast-coast. Our highly trained kiosk Advisors provide unbiased solutions  to some of the most engaged, affluent and loyal consumers in the country. So, it stands to reason that if we are serving the best of the best clientele, we only hire the best of the best leaders to run our business.

Director Role

Lead leaders. Shape culture. Drive transformation. Build the future!!

We view performance results as an OUTPUT.

OUTPUTS are delivered through actions, behaviors and activity – which we call INPUTS

Too often, we see sales associates and sales managers chasing outputs, which are sometimes known as KPI’s and pushing employees into “closing” customers. We have also seen that this “push” promotes solutions that do not fit what the customer actually needs. This short-term thinking approach we view as unsustainable and does not promote medium to long term growth

Our view is based upon focusing on INPUTS and we are strong believers that if you do the right thing, with the right people, in the right way, at the right time – you will invariably get the right result – the OUTPUT. We also strongly believe that OUTPUTS driven by proper INPUTS, provide the foundation for sustainable on-going growth.

The Director of Retail Operations is a leadership role which requires the right candidate to be able to operate both strategically and tactically (based upon the needs of our business) and is responsible for executing our operational go to market strategy.

Our team across the country is 600+ strong and they are the backbone of our operations. You will be responsible for leading our Western Canadian employees and growing our business through INFLUENCE, building CONSTITUENCY and showing your IMPACT through superior EXECUTION.

The key to winning at retail is the quality of our front-line people. Finding, recruiting, training and successfully onboarding is the foundation of any retailer’s success. This requires us to have hiring clarity on the profile of individual that we are looking for as well as determining who is a suitable candidate and who is not. We have found that this is key to developing and properly casting new hires into roles that match their strengths.

You will report into the Senior Director of Operation and be responsible for leading our business in 40+ locations and will be supporting 3 District Managers. This role requires you to be accountable for creating a high-performance culture where behaviors, execution and results are aligned. You will support our over-arching strategy and with the help of your leadership team, execute the tactical plan developed. You will drive organizational effectiveness (and change, where required) and ensures the creation of sustainable success by developing a strong leadership bench, identifying future talent, and guiding your teams through cyclical periods of growth, transformation, and change.

The ideal candidate must be influential and has impact when they communicate and are able to build constituency with other stakeholders and who can balance strategy with high levels of execution. The ideal candidate will also be able to challenge the status quo, can make difficult decisions, and inspire others to embrace change, while remaining focused and true to the execution of our strategy and operational plan.

What You Will Shine At

Leading and developing a team of District Managers and field leaders across a large and complex geographic region.
Driving organizational performance through strategic execution, accountability, and operational excellence.
Building leadership capability at all levels through coaching, mentorship, and succession planning.
Identifying opportunities to improve productivity, effectiveness, and business outcomes across the region.
Creating a culture of high performance, continuous improvement & accountability
Developing and executing talent strategies that attract, retain, and advance top performers.
Challenging leaders to think differently, improve execution, and raise performance standards.
Strengthening partnerships with Costco leadership through credibility, trust, and a shared commitment to delivering a world-class member experience.

Who You Are

You have 10+ years of progressive leadership experience leading large, multi-site teams through other leaders.
You have a proven track record of improving business performance through people, process, and execution.
You are an exceptional “change leader” who can create alignment, navigate ambiguity, and help teams embrace new ways of working.
You have successfully led organizational transformations, restructures, large-scale business initiatives, or performance turnarounds.
You are skilled at developing District Managers, senior leaders, and high-potential talent.
You hold leaders accountable while maintaining engagement, trust, and strong working relationships.
You inspire trust, create followership, and lead with integrity.
You have demonstrated success building leadership pipelines and developing future-ready organizations.

Your Playground

How You’ll Stand Out

Applicants should be prepared to:

Share examples of leading through significant organizational change while maintaining employee engagement and business performance.
Demonstrate how they have improved underperforming regions, districts, or business units.
Describe how they have built leadership capability and prepared future leaders for advancement.
Showcase examples of transforming team culture and creating sustainable accountability.
Explain how they have influenced senior stakeholders and aligned diverse teams behind a common vision.
Illustrate their approach to succession planning, talent reviews, and leadership development.
Share examples of making difficult decisions that strengthened long-term organizational effectiveness.

Benefits That Actually Matter

Total compensation package - $180K - $200K+
Excellent extended health benefits
RRSP company match program
Discounts on the newest wireless technology and plans
LinkedIn Learning
Maternity Leave Top-Up Program
Career growth opportunities within one of Canada's leading retail organizations
A chance to directly shape strategy, culture, leadership capability, and the future of the business

jobs.description:
Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Business - Infrastructure

Brookfield Infrastructure Group is one of Brookfield’s primary operating groups. The Infrastructure Group is one of the world’s largest infrastructure investors, owning and operating critical assets across the transport, utilities, energy, and data infrastructure sectors. The Group operates and manages approximately $262 billion of assets owned through its private funds and publicly listed entity, Brookfield Infrastructure Partners. Our portfolio of assets facilitate the movement and storage of energy, water, freight, passengers and data, and are located in North and South America, Europe and the Asia Pacific regions. For more information, visit: https://www.brookfield.com/our-businesses/infrastructure

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

Primary Responsibilities

Support the liquidity management process, staying abreast of investment and capital recycling activity and helping to keep senior management informed through weekly/quarterly reporting
Support the credit ratings process, including analysis of rating methodologies and preparing materials for rating agency presentations
Support financial risk management activities, including risk reporting, assisting with devising strategies to hedge foreign exchange and interest rate risk, and coordinating hedge execution
Support external financing activities for the public entity and its subsidiaries, in debt and equity capital markets transactions
Manage reporting of comprehensive treasury and risk management materials on a quarterly basis, provided to the Board and senior management across the organization
Remain well-informed of capital markets and Brookfield’s investment strategies
Prepare ad-hoc analysis and participate in ad-hoc projects as required

Degree in finance, accounting, or related business discipline
Completed CPA, CFA or related designation is an asset
Minimum 5+ years of experience in Finance (including accounting treasury, corporate finance and/or capital markets)
Self-motivated and proactive, with respect to both managing workload and professional development
Team player with positive attitude and willingness to adapt to changing work priorities
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, can work effectively with all levels and departments within a complex organization
Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, can simplify complex issues and provide solutions or recommendations in a clear and concise manner

Compensation Range: $165,000 - $185,000CAD

New Position

At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a competitive compensation and benefits package and excellent opportunities for growth and advancement. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and respect, value and welcome diversity in our workplace. Husky Technologies TM also values being a great place to work and strives to maintain a safe workplace. Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

Husky TechnologiesTM is committed to developing inclusive, barrier-free selection processes and work environments. jobs.title: Director, Product Management Equipment
jobs.description:
Join CoolIT, an Ecolab Company, a global leader in Direct Liquid Cooling technology for data centers, supercomputers, and high-performance computing environments.

The Director, Product Management – Equipment
leads the Data Center Equipment product line, with responsibility for Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs) and Technology Cooling System (TCS) piping. This role owns the equipment strategy, portfolio architecture, product roadmap, business performance, and lifecycle governance.

The Director leads the CDU Product Manager and Senior Manager, Product Management CDUs. Together, the team manages the full CDU portfolio through clearly defined ownership across programs, customers, and workstreams while maintaining one integrated roadmap and shared priorities. Until portfolio scale supports a dedicated TCS Piping Product Manager, ownership of TCS piping and CDU systems will remain integrated within the CDU product team.

What You Will Do

Own the global strategy, portfolio architecture, product roadmap, and financial performance of the Data Center Equipment product line, including the full CDU portfolio and TCS piping.
Lead and develop the CDU product management team, establishing clear ownership across programs, customers, and workstreams while maintaining one integrated roadmap, shared priorities, and coordinated decision-making.
Set portfolio priorities across growth platforms, strategic customer programs, new product introduction, sustainment, cost reduction, quality, supply continuity, regulatory requirements, and end-of-life.
Lead portfolio and phase-gate decisions using customer evidence, strategic alignment, business cases, technical and operational readiness, serviceability, risk, scalability, and lifecycle economics.
Partner with Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, Service, Sales, Finance, and Product Marketing to translate portfolio strategy into funded roadmaps, executable development programs, and successful product launches.
Define offering boundaries and system architecture across CDU hardware, TCS piping, controls, monitoring, coolant, commissioning, and lifecycle services.
Own market segmentation, competitive positioning, pricing architecture, margin improvement, revenue outlook, and portfolio performance while engaging strategic customers and ecosystem partners to identify future requirements for high-density, liquid-cooled data centers.
Establish and monitor portfolio KPIs, including revenue, gross margin, growth, win rate, roadmap delivery, launch performance, quality, cost, installed-base performance, and services pull-through.
Establish and govern the Equipment product-development operating system, including opportunity intake, business cases, requirements, prioritization, phase gates, development, verification and validation, launch readiness, sustainment, product changes, and end-of-life.
Establish product-management governance and documentation standards, including required deliverables, ownership, review cadence, approval criteria, decision rights, escalation paths, change control, systems of record, and traceability from customer requirements through development, validation, release, and lifecycle changes.
Lead recurring portfolio and product-development reviews to drive timely decisions, clear accountability, issue resolution, and effective execution while monitoring adherence to product-management processes.
Determine when portfolio scale, workload, and organizational maturity justify dedicated TCS Piping product-management ownership and lead an orderly transition of responsibilities.

Position Details

The position is based in CoolIT Headquarters, Calgary, AB.
The position requires travel of up to 10%, including international travel

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering.
12 years of experience in product management, product leadership, engineering, or commercialization of complex industrial or mission-critical equipment.
5 years of experience leading product managers or comparable cross-functional product teams.
Demonstrated experience owning portfolio strategy, product roadmaps, business cases, pricing, product-line financial performance, new product introduction, and lifecycle management.
Experience leading decisions across Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, Service, Sales, Finance, and regional organizations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with data center thermal management, liquid cooling, CDUs, piping, pumps, heat exchangers, controls, or related infrastructure.
Knowledge of standard, configurable, and engineered-to-order equipment business models.
Experience serving hyperscalers, colocation providers, original equipment manufacturers, engineering, procurement and construction firms, contractors, or mechanical, electrical and plumbing consultants.
Experience building product organizations, defining decision rights, and introducing specialized product ownership as a portfolio grows.
MBA or advanced technical degree.
Strong customer and commercial judgment, with the ability to distinguish scalable market needs from isolated requests, make clear portfolio trade-offs, and connect roadmap decisions to customer value, revenue, margin, adoption, and long-term portfolio performance.
Strong systems thinking across equipment, fluids, controls, digital capabilities, services, and lifecycle economics.
Proven ability to create clarity across technical, commercial, operational, and regional teams and translate strategy into prioritized decisions, successful launches, measurable performance, and sustained results.

We thank every candidate in advance; however, we will contact only those selected for an interview. Please note: immigration sponsorship is not available for this role.

Successful candidates for this position will be required to undergo background checks, including criminal record checks and education verification.

About Coolit, An Ecolab Company

Founded in Calgary, Alberta in 2001, CoolIT Systems is the leading Direct Liquid Cooling technology provider for data centers, supercomputers, and desktop computers. We design and manufacture solutions used by the largest tech companies globally.

Recognized as one of “The Americas’ Fastest Growing Companies 2023” by Financial Times and honored with the Deloitte Fast 50 Clean Technology award in 2022, as well as the Deloitte Fast 500 distinction in both 2021 and 2022, CoolIT's rapid growth is capturing global attention.

As demand for generative AI, high-performance computing and cloud solutions rapidly expands, there has never been a more exciting time to join our team.

During pre-screening, we may use an AI tool, supported by human oversight, to efficiently manage tasks such as resume screening and/or interview scheduling. All hiring decisions are made by human reviewers.

Successful candidates will be required to undergo pre-hire background checks as a condition of employment.

Our Commitment to a Culture of Inclusion & Belonging

Ecolab is committed to fair and equal treatment of associates and applicants and furthering the principles of Equal Opportunity to Employment. We will recruit, hire, promote, transfer and provide opportunities for advancement based on individual qualifications and job performance in all matters affecting employment, compensation, benefits, working conditions, and opportunities for advancement. Ecolab will not discriminate against any associate or applicant for employment because of race, religion, color, creed, national origin,citizenship status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expressions, genetic information, marital status, age, or disability.
